This game is either really hard or really easy. It depends on your reflexes and, to a certain degree, your luck.

Risk of Rain is a lot of fun if you're willing to sink some time into it and unlock some things. Unlocking things is done by playing through the game and completing tasks - some easy, some time consuming, and some that truly test the limits of your skill. Unfortunately in order to unlock every item, you have to be good with every character. There's more than a few item unlocks that require you to go undamaged for an amount of time, and that's quite a task when there's enemies everywhere. 

Now, the items I'm talking about. You've got two types of items - use items and passive items. Naturally you can only have one use item, and the variety of use items will often keep you wondering which would be better at the moment... Early on I prefer a disposable rocket launcher, but later, when I have the cooldown low enough to make it indefinite, I prefer to make my character invincible 100% of the time. Passive items, on the other hand, you can have an indefinite amount of - you can have one of each, or a hundred of each, up to the point of breaking your computer. Much of your damage and survivability in this is determined by the items you've picked up throughout that run. And since death is permanent, you don't get to keep any of the items if you screw up - you start over from the beginning, much like a newborn, naked and screaming in an unforgiving world. 

Characters are each relatively unique, and they all have their own playstyle. Items that are overpowered on one character might be completely useless on another, and monsters that you found easy when you could hit and run may be more difficult when you play someone who's less mobile. Every character has their strengths and weaknesses, and they're all different enough to feel like their own entities. Two characters may be good at the same thing, but the way they go about it may render items that were amazing for one useless on the other. An example - Commando and Huntress both play a multi-target hit-and-run style. Commando has higher attack speed and a skill that gives him some precious seconds of invulnerability, but the Huntress is capable of movement while attacking, making her more reliant on movement speed items than the Commando, who would prefer lots of extra attack speed and on-hit effects. And not everyone is ranged either - you have melee characters as well which, personall, I find to be too difficult for my tastes, but are in their own right powerful. One is a DPS monster who's cenetered on Damage over Time, another who's got more mobility than damage. Every character has their strengths and their weaknesses, and they all, to a certain degree, require you to be skilled with their use... some more than others. 

The final mechanic, and the one that more often keeps people coming back, is the artifact system. Artifacts, much like items, can be picked up in the field. Unlike items, though, their effects can't be used until you return to the menu - live or die. When choosing your character, any artifact you found in any prior playthrough can be used to change the way the game is played. One that eliminates chests, forcing you to look to the endless horde for your loot, or another that renders you an unstoppable force of destruction with skin made of paper - one hit to kill, one hit to be killed. Artifacts can be combined, as well, and one of them even requires you to do one run, all the way through to the final boss, with every other relic active. The artifact system allows you to change the way the game is played to suit your mood, whenever you feel you need the change. Just be careful what you wish for, not all artifacts are meant to make your life easier.
